items.title: Ramsey Lewis — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Michael [?Kochs], who is an artist-designer in his own right, with his own company, who works with me sometimes.

ctx.x: Maybe we could talk about the piece that seemed to be most representative of your philosophy or your humanitarian outlook, and that is Colors. Talk about that piece, how that came about, and how you feel about that piece.

The Evolution of – Colors: the Evolution [sic: Ecology] of Oneness – actually, Guthrie Ramsey came up with the name after I had been talking with Michael [?Kochs], who is an artist-designer in his own right, with his own company, who works with me sometimes. He – Michael – had asked me, what’s going to be your next? I felt that bringing people together was important to me. To write some music that inspired people to think in terms of themselves as part of the human race, rather – first, before they thought in…
University. We sat there, Guthrie and the gentleman from Loyola, who’s going to kill me when he sees this and I didn’t use his name. Stop, because this – I got to do it.
